# Summary interpretation

With the plot we'll interpret the results of *Cutibacterium acnes* and some overall patterns.

<center>
![](images/summary_plot.png){style="width:800px"}
</center>
<br>

### *C.acnes*

*Cutibacterium acnes* is the top feature in the plot so lets discuss what the plot can tell us.

The top associations are the abundance associations for cheek and scalp.
We can see both their coefficients are higher than the median coefficient via the circles in the coefficient plot.
Additionally, these circle are dark purple indicating high significance (q-value < 0.1).

Interestingly the coefficients of the prevalence models are high but not significant (>0.1).
This seems strange due to the fact the coefficient values are the largest in the coefficient plot (>10).

To find out why this is we can look in the `significant_results.html` and search for `Cutibacterium acnes`.
Carry this out and you'll see four rows, 2 for the cheek and scalp abundance modelling and 2 for their prevalence modelling.
The individual q-values for the prevalence modelling are both 0.
What's causing this lack of significance?

In this case it is lack of power.
The column `N_not_zero` shows 170 out of the 172 samples have the feature present.
With only 2 samples not containing the feature the prevalence association test does not have enough power to give a significant result.

Why is the coefficient so large then?
This can occur in logistics modelling when the feature is present in all the query samples but absent in only a few reference samples.
The other way round can cause highly negative coefficient values.

:::{.callout-note}
In your own analysis you may need to look at all the results `all_results.tsv` to find feature associations that are not present in the significant results output.
:::

### Overall

Some overall patterns to notice are:

- Scalp versus axilla has similar results to cheek versus axilla, axilla was a good reference to choose
- The top five features have strong positive coefficients for abundance for the scalp and cheek comparisons
- The middle features (*G.adiacens* to *L.mirabilis*, except *S.capitis*) have higher prevalence in the cheek samples compared to axilla
- The bottom features (*A.octavius* to *C.pseudokroppenstedtii*) are in lower abundance in the scalp and cheek samples compared to the axilla samples
- Features where prevalence is more likely with higher read depths also seem to have associations of lower prevalence in the TimepointNamePool_visit7,8,9
- There are no significant abundance associations for Reads or TimepointNamePool_visits7,8,9

That's been a lot but we have even more!
